patients.label: Boy with cryptogenic cirrhosis and severe hepatopulmonary syndrome with a hepatic hemangioma, first admitted at 8 months and followed to 4 years
attribution_limitations: The case section calls the echocardiogram transesophageal, while the discussion calls the saline bubble test contrast-enhanced transthoracic echocardiography "as done in our patient".
HIV-DNA PCR is said to be negative at 18 months of age, although the case narrative is at 8 months and then 4 years and the neonatal sentence appears before the 8-month admission.

The text reports raised creatinine and urea at the 8-month admission, while Table 1 lists creatinine 83.7 against a printed interval of 88−176 and urea 22 against 7–14. The text and table values are not merged (the table has no cell flags).

Units differ in notation between text and Table 1 for the 4-year platelet count (text "× 109/L", table "× 10^(3)/mL"); Table 1 value cells carry no unit and some row labels print units inside the reference interval only.

The hemangioma was not found at exploration or on the wedge biopsy; the discussion says it did not increase in size, was not found on laparotomy, and most likely underwent spontaneous resolution. The case narrative calls the operation an exploration and the discussion calls it a laparotomy; the source does not state they are the same event.

The case section states the patient was assessed as having cryptogenic cirrhosis, while the discussion says he most likely had cryptogenic cirrhosis based on physical findings and nonconclusive results.

The article defines very severe hepatopulmonary syndrome as PaO2 < 50 mmHg, while the case reports PaO2 < 34 mmHg and calls the syndrome severe; the discussion also notes pulmonary vascular dilatation could not be confirmed by angiography or a nuclear study.

The discussion says the patient had two admissions in infancy due to severe illnesses with unfound aetiology and investigations that did not point towards immunodeficiency; the case section describes admissions at 3 months and 8 months, but the source does not state these are the two.

The scanned cardiology report image in supplement f1 (pixel content, not facts) words the age at the cardiology consultation, the onset of abdominal distension, the age at hemangioma diagnosis and the organ sizes on examination differently from the case text, and calls the operation a laparotomy. These describe a different encounter or a retrospective history, not the same measurements as the text facts, so the text facts are kept and nothing is reconciled.
It is not stated from what event the additional 2.5 years of survival is counted.

Table 1 prints units and reference intervals whose magnitudes do not fit several values: total bilirubin is labelled µmol/L with an interval of <17.1 but values of 0.8 and 0.53; total protein and albumin intervals are printed in mg/dL; WBC and platelet intervals are printed per mL; the creatinine interval is 88−176 µmol/L. Values and units are copied as printed.
The discussion says confirmation "with pulmonary angiography or technetium-99m MAA nuclear study" could not be done; the "X or Y" wording does not separate the two studies.

Several steps of the 4-year work-up have no order words: the suspicion of hepatopulmonary syndrome is tied to the 4-year examination only by diagnostic basis wording ("With these examination and laboratory findings"), the echocardiography is not ordered against the CT, exploration or biopsy, the wedge biopsy is not stated to have been taken at the exploration, and the final assessment cites its basis ("in view of").
